description: A trigger sequencer of sixteen rows over sixteen patterns, each row a line of hexadecimal digits where every digit is four steps

params.text: Picks which of the sixteen patterns is played and edited
Copies the sixteen rows of the pattern being edited
Writes the copied rows into the pattern being edited

inputs.text: Each trigger here takes the sequence one step on
A trigger here puts every row back to its first step
Picks the pattern by cable: with Pattern Poly Select on, a trigger on a channel of this jack chooses the pattern of that number, and with it off the voltage chooses, 0.625V per pattern over 0-10V

outputs.text: A 10ms trigger on the channel of each row whose step is a one bit
Carries 10V on the channel of each row whose step is a one bit, held until the next step
Passes the clock through on the channel of each row whose step is a one bit
A 10ms trigger on the channel of each row whose step is a zero bit

notes: a row does nothing until digits are typed into its field and entered; the text is red while it is being edited and green once it counts
each digit is read as four steps from its four bits, so 8 is a step on the beat, 2 the usual hi-hat and 08 the usual snare
an asterisk in place of a digit is picked afresh at random every time it comes round
a row loops on its own length, four steps per digit, so rows of different lengths drift against each other
changing pattern, by knob or by cable, also puts the sequence back to its first step
in a field, p fills it at random, r and l roll the bits right and left, and h spreads each digit over two; adding shift enters the result at once
the maker marks this module as superseded and points to HexSeqP2 in another of his plugins
menu: Pattern Poly Select — chooses which way the Pat jack picks a pattern: on, a trigger on a channel of it; off, the voltage at it
ShowLights — turns the row of lamps above each field on or off; the lit lamp is the digit being played
Clock In Delay — holds each clock back by that many samples before the step is taken, 0 to 15, which is a way of letting a reset land first
Random — opens a slider setting how many bits a random fill switches on, 0 to 100 per cent
Random length from — sets the fewest digits a random fill writes, 1 to 16
Random length to — sets the most digits a random fill writes, 1 to 16
Randomize Pattern — fills every row of the pattern being edited at random, at that density and those lengths
Initialize Pattern — empties every row of the pattern being edited

inputs.0: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.1: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.2:
0 to 10V · stepped · polyphonic

unpatched it reads the Pat knob; a negative voltage does nothing here.
